title: Quantitative imaging of single-cell phenotypes in cancer cells cultured on hydrogel surfaces
protocol: Label WM266-4 cells with CellTracker Orange CMTMR dye the day before transfections.
Remove growth medium from flasks and wash cells twice with PBS.
Dilute CellTracker in DMEM (1:10,000) without FBS.
Add diluted CellTracker to cells at 10 mL per 75 cm² flask.
Incubate flasks for 30 min at 37°C with 5% CO₂.
Remove medium containing CellTracker and wash cells once with PBS.
Add fresh medium with 10% FBS and 5% penicillin/streptomycin to the cells.
Prior to seeding cells, add 20 μL/well of OptiMEM (Invitrogen) into assay plates.
Mix each well with 160 nL/well Lipofectamine RNAiMAX (Invitrogen).
Incubate plates for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Seed approximately 5,000 cells/well in 80 μL of complete medium for all wells containing siRNA and a subset of control wells.
Incubate plates with transfected cells for 24 h at 37°C.
Prepare rat tail type I collagen mix on ice: Add HEPES buffer last and check the pH is 7.5.
Mix collagen slowly to avoid introducing bubbles.
Pour collagen mix into a reagent reservoir on ice and aliquot 100 μL collagen mix into 96 well cell carrier imaging plates.
Spin plates at 112 × g and place in an incubator at 37°C for 1 h.
If not used that day, store the plates in the fridge.
Lift transfected cells by trypsinization: Add 20 μL trypsin-EDTA (0.25%)/well for 1 min and then add 80 μL medium/well.
Transfer 100 μL transfected cells in medium on top of 100 μL/well rat tail type I polymerized collagen.
Spin cells on top of collagen at 112 × g for 2 min and incubate plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Fix cells after 24 h incubation by adding 100 μL of pre-warmed 8% methanol-free formaldehyde containing 5 μg/mL Hoechst stain and incubate for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Set up the microscope settings and place plate into the imaging platform.
Define the plate type (96 well cell carrier plates).
Select the appropriate objective, lasers and filters.
Determine microscope settings, exposure time and z-positions.
Select a well and find focus height using the Z-stack.
Cells are found at different planes so determine the bottom of the stack and start imaging in depths of approximately 350–600 μm.
Image plates with a high NA 20× air immersion objective.
Define the plate layout and number of fields per well (15 fields per well).
Save experimental design.
Go to run experiment, name it, and start the run.
After the run is finished import data into the Columbus analysis software.
